body:
I think this should be renamed to something like `ordered_self_setget_properties` to make it clear that it is only for those kinds of properties. 
Ideally, we wouldn't need something like this, but that would require updating the `ClassDB` hashing function to retrieve all property types at once, whether they are setgets, signals, etc. If we do that and need order preservation, then the maps should be `HashMap` and not `AHashMap` to preserve insertion order.
This is the first time I've seen an initialization inside an if in the codebase, which, if true, warrants discussion about whether the codebase should allow/adopt that style.
Removing this nesting would be better too, and it can be achieved by moving the check for `free_` first.
Do we still need all of the above maps (methods, signals, constants), considering everything gets stored in the property map now? Looks like duplicated storage to me.

I agree it's not the best name, but the elements are not just `setget` properties. Property groups etc. are also added here.
I think it's only useful for the editor, so this is a list of 'inspector properties'. Not sure what a good name for this would be.

I somehow dislike 'polluting' a scope with temporary variables as it can lead to bugs.
But yea we don't have many uses like this so it's good to highlight it in case somebody wants to disagree to this style.

Usually I agree, but in this case it's consistent with `get_native`, where `property != nullptr` case isn't the only case; `get_native` has a special case for `free_` (which tbh probably shouldn't....).
That would make it slightly slower in the happy path, since almost no `get_native` calls will enter the `free_` path.
Yea I'm considering reduce this down again but doing this now would explode the diff, so my OP lists it as a possible follow-up.

As you highlight above, and I agree with, there probably shouldn't be a `free_` case, which would enable removal of the unhappy path, and thus allow the unnesting of both. What would stand against removing the `free_` case?
I definitely agree we should adress it in a follow-up, reasoning for not doing it now makes sense.
I don't have context for it and just removing it will probably break compat

`ordered_inspector_properties`? 
Not a big fan of editor code being in `GDType`... can't really have it any other way, though, can we? Unless we add a bookkeeping location somewhere in `editor/`. Sounds not much better though.
Ok so it is what it is, I guess. Maybe a follow-up can adress it.

Yea me neither but addressing that would be more refactor than excusable atm.
Your name sounds fine though I'll need to check if that's actually the only use case
Oh yeah any such refactor would be a separate PR.
I'm confused as to why this is in here.

The PR rejects name conflicts harder than previously. `reparent` is a function on `Node` so `ReparentDialog ` adding a signal with this name creates a conflict. 
In exposed code this would mean that either of the two would not be accessible via `dialog.reparent`. In the new implementation it means that the map would not accurately reflect all known properties (dropping either the signal or the method).
I'm not necessarily looking to keep this functionality, but why is it removed in this PR? Can the GDType not support this? Do we need this for anything?

The boolean was used in two places, which now handle the functionality in-line because it's not a typing concern but an editor concern.
It's the 4th (last) bullet in the "Additional information" section.
Seems like it's already being used https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9ba32b09e0dfa4a6c1b82312554894615c716cce/core/variant/container_type_validate.h#L116
